chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassha', from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Salamah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Two 'Eids coincided during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), so he addressed the people and said: 'This is a day on which two 'Eids have coincided. Whoever wishes to join us (in prayer) should do so, and whoever does not do so, he has a concession (rukhsah).' He meant whoever was staying away (from the congregation).

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two Eid prayers coincide on the same day?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *Jam'* (combining) the two Eid prayers when they fall on the same day, attributing the precedent to Imam Ali (AS) during the Prophet's time. It highlights the principle of *rukhsa* (concession), allowing individuals who prefer to pray separately or are otherwise occupied the flexibility to do so without penalty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease in worship. The narration underscores the communal nature of the Eid prayer while respecting individual circumstances.
